findings.title: Missing double-check after acquiring write lock causes redundant work
findings.body: After acquiring the write lock (line 48-49), the code does not re-check whether entryPointAssetsCache is already populated and the environment is non-Dev before redoing the (potentially expensive) file/CDN read. Multiple goroutines that pass the initial RLock check with ret == nil (e.g. at startup, before the cache has been populated) will each serialize on the write lock and redundantly re-read the manifest file or re-fetch from the CDN, overwriting the cache with the same result each time. This defeats much of the purpose of caching for concurrent initial requests and can add unnecessary I/O latency under load. The fix should re-check `cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil` right after acquiring the write lock and return early if so.

findings.title: No test added to verify the data race fix
findings.body: This PR's stated purpose is fixing a data race in GetWebAssets, but no test (e.g. a concurrent-call test runnable with `go test -race`) was added to verify that the race is actually fixed or to guard against regressions. Without such a test, a future refactor could silently reintroduce the race on the shared entryPointAssetsCache global.
